title: DRAEM: A discriminatively trained reconstruction embedding for surface anomaly detection
mechanism: Perlin-noise masks blend outside textures (DTD) into normal images. A reconstruction network plus a discriminative network is trained to segment these synthetic anomalies.
evidence: Beat prior unsupervised methods on MVTec AD by a large margin. On DAGM its localisation beats fully supervised methods (abstract). The repo is MIT-licensed and uses DTD as the anomaly source.
adaptation: For the benchmark, run it as the 'no defect labels' baseline: train on crack-free train cells, then score crack and inactive AP and relF1@2 on test and E1. For scores, replace DTD textures with dark-line and dark-blob primitives; this is a long shot.
min_experiment: DRAEM trained on crack-free train cells. Report crack and inactive AP and relF1@2 on test and E1. No kill line (benchmark baseline). Score arm: PF + DRAEM map as a second input channel vs PF, kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark no-defect-label baseline trained on crack-free train cells; for scores, swap DTD textures for dark-line and dark-blob primitives.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run: crack / inactive AP and relF1@2 on test and E1; no kill.
